propositions.text: The appellant is a Uruguayan citizen and Argentine permanent resident; his wife and children are Argentine citizens.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Uruguay and a permanent resident of Argentina. His wife, XXXX XXXX XXXX, and their minor children, XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX, are citizens of Argentina.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant is a Uruguayan citizen and Argentine permanent resident; his wife and children are Argentine citizens, court states.

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the wife as the designated representative of her minor children.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) confirms XXXX XXXX XXXX as the designated representative of her minor children.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the wife as the designated representative of her minor children, court states.

propositions.text: The appellants appeal the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claims as not meeting IRPA definitions.
propositions.quote: The appellants are appealing the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting their claims for refugee protection. The RPD determined that they are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The appellants appeal the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claims as not meeting IRPA definitions, court states.

propositions.text: The appellants filed no new documents or request for hearing but ask RAD to set aside RPD's decision and allow their claims.
propositions.quote: The appellants filed no new documents in support of their appeal, and they are not requesting a hearing before the RAD. The appellants are asking the RAD to set aside the RPD's determination and allow their claims for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants filed no new documents or request hearing but ask RAD to set aside RPD's decision and allow claims, appellants say.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA, the RAD sets aside the RPD's determination that the appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(c) of the IRPA, the RAD sets aside the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are not "Convention refugees" under section 96 of the IRPA or "persons in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD sets aside the RPD's determination that the appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection, court orders.

propositions.text: The appeal is allowed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is allowed, court states.

propositions.text: Before leaving Argentina in 2016, the male appellant lived in Moreno, Buenos Aires, working as a dental surgeon with his wife as receptionist.
propositions.quote: Before he left Argentina in March 2016, the male appellant and his family were living in Moreno, a suburb of the capital city, Buenos Aires. He was a dental surgeon and owned his own practice in central Moreno. His wife worked with him as a receptionist.

paragraphs.summary: Before leaving Argentina in 2016, the male appellant lived in Moreno, Buenos Aires, working as a dental surgeon with his wife as receptionist, court states.

propositions.text: The male appellant initially served a disadvantaged neighborhood including many gypsies; wife also worked elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The male appellant states in his Basis of Claim Form that he initially became established in a disadvantaged neighbourhood (XXXX XXXX XXXX) in order to offer his services to a less wealthy segment of the population, which included a large number of gypsies. His wife's written narrative indicates that they were also working elsewhere at the same time.

paragraphs.summary: The male appellant initially served a disadvantaged neighborhood including many gypsies; wife also worked elsewhere, appellants say.

propositions.text: The gypsy community demanded more free services; the gypsy chief and son threatened to kill the male appellant.
propositions.quote: The male appellant stated that, as the years went on, the gypsy community demanded that he provide more and more services free of charge. The male appellant alleged that the gypsy chief (the cacique) and his son XXXX intimidated him and threatened to kill him when he told them he had no openings to treat them or when he had to refer gypsy patients to colleagues for more specialized care.

paragraphs.summary: The gypsy community demanded more free services; the gypsy chief and son threatened to kill the male appellant, appellants say.

propositions.text: In 2009, after threats, they told wife's father, who said authorities need witness or evidence to act.
propositions.quote: In 2009, after XXXX threatened to kill him, they told the female appellant's father (a retired police officer) about their problems. He explained that the authorities would not accept their complaint without a witness or evidence.

propositions.text: They moved to central Moreno hoping for fewer problems, but gypsies continued to pressure for free or barter services.
propositions.quote: The appellants left XXXX XXXX XXXX for central Moreno, where they believed they would have fewer problems. However, the situation did not improve; the gypsies continued to pressure the male appellant to provide his services free of charge, or in exchange for goods.

paragraphs.summary: After threats, they told wife's father who said authorities need evidence; they moved but gypsies still pressured for free services, appellants say.

propositions.text: The wife received a call falsely claiming husband was held hostage demanding ransom; sister-in-law also victim of virtual kidnapping.
propositions.quote: The male appellant alleged that his wife received a telephone call from someone falsely claiming that her husband was being held hostage and demanding a ransom. A sister-in-law was allegedly also a victim of such a virtual kidnapping scheme.

paragraphs.summary: The wife received a false hostage ransom call; sister-in-law also victim of virtual kidnapping, appellants allege.

propositions.text: The wife was near school when a car occupant tried to abduct a child among mothers and children.
propositions.quote: The male appellant further alleges that his wife was near the school one day, along with other mothers and their children, when a car drove up to them and one of the occupants tried to abduct one of the children.

paragraphs.summary: The wife was near school when a car occupant tried to abduct a child, appellants allege.

propositions.text: In 2014, they considered moving to Uruguay but learned gypsies travel freely there and child abductions occur.
propositions.quote: In 2014, the appellants considered leaving Argentina and moving to Uruguay, but the male appellant's family told them it was not the best option. The appellants allegedly learned that gypsies travel freely between the two countries and that there have been child abductions in Uruguay, as well as drug problems.

paragraphs.summary: In 2014, they considered moving to Uruguay but learned gypsies travel freely there and child abductions occur, appellants say.

propositions.text: They wanted to leave Argentina, applied to Finland but refused, closed practice, got US visa, then came to Canada to claim refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The appellants wanted to leave Argentina. They submitted an application to go to Finland, but were refused. The male appellant closed his practice at the end of 2015. They obtained a visa allowing them to travel to the United States, then came to Canada to claim refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: They wanted to leave Argentina, applied to Finland but refused, closed practice, got US visa, then came to Canada to claim refugee protection, appellants say.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellants credibly provided dental services to gypsies who used intimidation to demand more services.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the appellants had credibly established that they had provided dental services to the gypsy community in Aurora, that this community had demanded more and more services, and that they had used intimidation to back up their demands.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellants endured the situation as long as possible but concluded male appellant could return to Uruguay.
propositions.quote: The RPD also found it credible that they had endured the situation for as long as they could. However, the RPD concluded that the male appellant could return to Uruguay.

propositions.text: The male appellant did not establish that proximity of Uruguay and gypsies there would enable threats to find him.
propositions.quote: The male appellant had not established that the proximity of Uruguay and the presence of gypsies in that country would enable "Cacique and XXXX" to find him there.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellants credibly provided dental services to gypsies who intimidated; concluded male appellant could return to Uruguay as threats unlikely to find him, RPD found.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded appellants have an internal flight alternative in Mendoza and it would be reasonable to move there.
propositions.quote: The RPD further concluded that, alternatively, the principal claimant and his family have an internal flight alternative (IFA) in Mendonza and that it would not be unreasonable for them to move there.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD concluded appellants have an internal flight alternative in Mendoza and it would be reasonable to move there, RPD found.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD erred in law by breaching procedural fairness by failing to provide adequate reasons.
propositions.quote: The appellants argue on appeal that the RPD's decision contains an error of law. They submit that the RPD committed a breach of procedural fairness by failing to provide adequate reasons for its decision.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD erred in law by breaching procedural fairness by failing to provide adequate reasons, appellants say.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in assessing corroborating evidence and in concluding they have a viable internal flight alternative.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the RPD erred in its assessment of the corroborating documentary evidence and in its conclusion that they have a viable IFA.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD erred in assessing corroborating evidence and concluding they have a viable internal flight alternative, appellants say.

propositions.text: The Federal Court of Appeal ruled in Huruglica that the RAD is a safety net correcting RPD mistakes on law or facts.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court of Appeal ruled in Huruglica1 on the scope of appeals before the RAD. In analyzing the legislative provisions and reiterating Parliament's intent in creating the RAD, Justice Gauthier remarked as follows: [98] The RAD was essentially viewed as the safety net that would catch all mistakes made by the RPD, be it on the law or the facts.

paragraphs.summary: The Federal Court of Appeal ruled in Huruglica that the RAD is a safety net correcting RPD mistakes on law or facts, court explains.

propositions.text: Findings of fact without credibility issues reviewed on correctness; credibility findings get some deference to RPD.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court of Appeal further ruled that findings of fact (and mixed fact and law), which raised no issue of credibility of oral evidence, must be reviewed applying the correctness standard. Where findings of fact or mixed fact and law require an assessment of the credibility or weight to be given to the oral evidence, the RPD may, in some cases, enjoy a meaningful advantage over the RAD. The Court of Appeal further ruled that the level of deference owed to the RPD in each case will vary and that the RAD should be given the opportunity to develop its own jurisprudence in that respect.

paragraphs.summary: Findings of fact without credibility issues reviewed on correctness; credibility findings get some deference to RPD, court explains.

propositions.text: RAD in X (Re) held that where deference to RPD findings is warranted, RAD applies a reasonableness standard adapted to its context
propositions.quote: Where deference to findings of the RPD is warranted, the standard of RAD reasonableness will be applied.

propositions.text: RPD's findings must be comprehensible so RAD can understand how conclusions were reached
propositions.quote: the RPD's findings must be "the result of a comprehensible reasoning process - the RAD must be able to read the RPD's decision and understand how the RPD's conclusion was reached."

propositions.text: RAD considers refugee determination on correctness standard even when deferring to some RPD findings
propositions.quote: The RAD will consider the refugee determination on a standard of correctness, even where it has deferred to some or all of the findings upon which that determination is based.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier RAD decision held that RAD applies a reasonableness standard with comprehensible reasoning but uses correctness for refugee determinations.

propositions.text: Paragraph 171(c) IRPA gives three-member RAD panel decisions precedential value like an appeal court's for a trial court
propositions.quote: Paragraph 171(c) of the IRPA states that a decision of a panel of three members of the RAD has, for the RPD and for a panel of one member of the RAD, the same precedential value as a decision of an appeal court has for a trial court.

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 171(c) IRPA gives three-member RAD panel decisions precedential value like an appeal court's for a trial court.

propositions.text: RAD will independently analyze evidence to determine if RPD erred as female appellant alleges
propositions.quote: the RAD will conduct an independent analysis of the evidence in order to determine whether the RPD erred as the female appellant alleges.

propositions.text: If RPD erred in fact, law, or mixed fact and law, RAD must intervene per IRPA sections 110 and 111
propositions.quote: If the RPD erred in fact, in law, or in mixed fact and law, the RAD must intervene in accordance with sections 110 and 111 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will independently analyze evidence and intervene if the RPD erred in fact, law, or mixed fact and law, per IRPA.

propositions.text: Claims must be examined under section 97, not section 96 of IRPA
propositions.quote: these claims for refugee protection must be examined in relation to section 97 rather than section 96 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: Section 96 requires well-founded fear based on Convention grounds, which appellant's free services to gypsies lack
propositions.quote: In order for section 96 to apply, the refugee protection claimant must have a well-founded fear based on one or more of the Convention grounds. The fact that the appellant provided professional services [translation] "free of charge" to gypsies has no nexus to any of the five Convention grounds.

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues claims must be examined under section 97, as appellant's free services to gypsies lack nexus to Convention grounds under section 96.

propositions.text: Supreme Court in Ward defined refugee protection's purpose and three categories of particular social group
propositions.quote: The Supreme Court stated in Ward2 that the purpose of refugee protection is to defend human rights and to combat discrimination. The Court also set out three possible categories of particular social group: * groups defined by an innate, unchangeable characteristic; * groups whose members voluntarily associate for reasons so fundamental to their human dignity that they should not be forced to forsake the association; and * groups associated by a former voluntary status, unalterable due to its historical permanence.

paragraphs.summary: The Supreme Court in Ward defined refugee protection's purpose and three categories of particular social group.

propositions.text: Appellant's free services to gypsies do not align with Supreme Court's refugee protection purpose
propositions.quote: The services the appellant provided to the gypsies, while laudable, do not correspond to the purpose the Supreme Court mentions in its decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's free services to gypsies do not align with Supreme Court's refugee protection purpose.

propositions.text: IFA is a mixed fact and law question reviewed on correctness standard when no credibility issue arises
propositions.quote: An IFA is a question of mixed fact and law that must be reviewed on a correctness standard when it raises no issue of credibility.

propositions.text: IFA in Mendonza, 800 km from Buenos Aires, is central to this refugee claim
propositions.quote: The IFA in Mendonza, a city located 800 kilometres from Buenos Aires, is at the heart of this claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states IFA in Mendonza is central and must be reviewed on correctness standard when no credibility issue arises.

propositions.text: Claims must be re-determined by RPD due to fatal error in second prong of IFA analysis
propositions.quote: these claims must be re-determined by the RPD. The decision contains a fatal error in the second prong of the IFA analysis.

propositions.text: Court cannot correct error without hearing and refers matter back to RPD
propositions.quote: I cannot correct this error without holding a hearing, and I must therefore refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds fatal error in IFA analysis and refers claims back to RPD for re-determination after hearing.

propositions.text: IFA analysis factors consider male appellant's relocation to Mendonza but he must show risk in Uruguay
propositions.quote: the factors considered in the IFA analysis are based on the fact that it would not be unreasonable for the male appellant and his family to relocate to that city. However, the male appellant is a citizen of Uruguay, and he must establish that he faces a prospective risk in his own country of citizenship.

propositions.text: IFA in Mendonza applies only if life is in danger in Uruguay
propositions.quote: The IFA in Mendonza should be considered only if it has been established that his life is in danger in Uruguay.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds IFA in Mendonza applies only if male appellant faces danger in Uruguay, his country of citizenship.

propositions.text: IFA in Mendonza is determinative only for female appellant and children, citizens of Argentina
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the IFA in Mendonza can only be determinative for the female appellant and the children, who are citizens of Argentina.

propositions.text: No evidence why Mendonza is not viable IFA for female appellant and children
propositions.quote: There is no evidence before me to show why Mendonza would not be a viable IFA for the female appellant and the children.

propositions.text: Female appellant was not questioned about relocating to Mendonza or working outside husband's practice
propositions.quote: she was not questioned about why she and the children could not move there, if she found work elsewhere than in her husband's practice.

propositions.text: This error is fatal to the second prong of the IFA analysis
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this error is fatal to the IFA analysis, specifically to the second prong of this analysis.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds IFA in Mendonza determinative only for female appellant and children, noting fatal error in IFA analysis second prong.

propositions.text: State protection in Argentina for female appellant and children is determinative issue
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the determinative issue in these claims is state protection in Argentina for the female appellant and the children.

propositions.text: State protection is also important issue in male appellant's claim
propositions.quote: I am also of the opinion that this is an important issue in the male appellant's claim.

propositions.text: Cannot rule on state protection without questioning appellants; testimony raises unresolved questions
propositions.quote: I cannot rule on this matter without questioning the appellants. The appellants' testimony regarding why they did not seek police protection in Argentina raises questions that I cannot resolve without a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds state protection in Argentina is key and cannot rule without questioning appellants due to unresolved testimony questions.

propositions.text: Set aside RPD's determination that appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under section 97 IRPA
propositions.quote: I set aside the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court sets aside RPD's determination that appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under section 97 IRPA.

propositions.text: Appeal is allowed
propositions.quote: The appeal is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the appeal.
